verify_text:
protocol.py: VERIFIED against plate map dil-03. 8 of 8 wells hold what the plate map says.
  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 1). Reading of the request: 8 standards;
    last well keeps 100 ul.

Labware for the technique (Serial dilution): nothing to flag.

Where every liquid ended up (ul):
  liquid                             declared delivered in source elsewhere    lost
  bsa                                   500.0     100.0     400.0       0.0     0.0
  water                                 500.0     350.0     150.0       0.0     0.0

Prep sheet: what to put on the deck before the run.
  slot labware                               well  liquid                       load at least  declared
  3    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5  A1    bsa                                  100.0     500.0
  3    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5  A2    water                                350.0     500.0
  Tips: 15 from Opentrons OT-2 96 Tip Rack 20 µL in slot 2.
  'Load at least' is what the robot draws. Add the dead volume of your tube or reservoir.

This checks the logic of the protocol: what goes where, and how much. It does not check the
  physics: whether a viscous liquid is pipetted accurately, or a drop stays on a tip.

check_text:
protocol.py: 2 biology problems (2 notes).

1. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No blank on a dilution series: 8 wells of bsa
   line 29:  p20.transfer(100, tuberack['A1'], dest, new_tip='never')
   At line 29 the robot starts a dilution series of bsa in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat
   (slot 1): 8 wells at 8 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than the one
   before. No well on this plate holds water with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve
   has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told
   from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 1.
   Fix: Add a well of water alone, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [2d2b517890f3]

2. NOTE CONTAM-WELL: A used tip carried water (tube A2 in slot 3) into well A1 in slot 1 it
was never meant for
   line 39:  p20.transfer(50, plate[std_wells[i-1]], dest, new_tip='never')
   At line 39 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 1 while it still carried water
   (tube A2 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into
   this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different
   samples, each now holds a little of another.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 1.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 39. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense
   from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is
   already in the well.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   [d13d77d7d1fc]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.explanation: At line 29 the robot starts a dilution series of bsa in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 1): 8 wells at 8 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than the one before. No well on this plate holds water with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 1.
findings.fix: Add a well of water alone, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: A used tip carried water (tube A2 in slot 3) into well A1 in slot 1 it was never meant for
findings.explanation: At line 39 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 1 while it still carried water (tube A2 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 39. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.
